Recent work shows that RL fine-tuning updates only 5--30\% of parameters~\citep{mukherjee2025rlsubnetworks}; whether CKA-based pruning preferentially preserves structures within this active subnetwork is an open question that would provide a complementary mechanistic explanation.

\paragraph{Why representational diversity may aid RL exploration.}
RLVR recovers pruned models through \emph{global exploration}---compressing incorrect reasoning paths while discovering alternative solutions~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}.
This process requires diverse computational pathways that can be repurposed through RL.
Gradient importance scoring retains structures optimized for the current loss landscape but removes representationally unique structures whose value lies not in their current contribution but in the non-redundant pathways they provide for future exploration.
CKA-based pruning inverts this priority: it sacrifices immediately ``useful'' but functionally redundant structures to preserve the structural diversity that RL exploration requires.
This connects to the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth}: the ``winning ticket'' depends on the training paradigm---a subnetwork optimal for SFT may lack the exploration diversity needed for RLVR.

\paragraph{Practical implications.}
Our results suggest two actionable guidelines for LLM compression pipelines that include RL-based recovery.

\paragraph{Why representational diversity may aid RL exploration.}
RLVR recovers pruned models through \emph{global exploration}---compressing incorrect reasoning paths while discovering alternative solutions~\citep{rlsqueezes2026}.
This process requires diverse computational pathways that can be repurposed through RL.
Gradient importance scoring retains structures optimized for the current loss landscape but removes representationally unique structures whose value lies not in their current contribution but in the non-redundant pathways they provide for future exploration.
CKA-based pruning inverts this priority: it sacrifices immediately ``useful'' but functionally redundant structures to preserve the structural diversity that RL exploration requires.
This connects to the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis~\citep{frankle2019lth}: the ``winning ticket'' depends on the training paradigm---a subnetwork optimal for SFT may lack the exploration diversity needed for RLVR.
